summary: 71-year-old man 6 years after open AAA repair with a Dacron graft: small haematemesis and melaena (herald bleed) that stopped, low-grade fever; HR 102, SBP 118, Hb 10.9. Must not be managed as a routine ulcer bleed: CT angiography and vascular surgery.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Vomited blood once and black stools
inputs.hpi: Vomited about half a cup of blood this morning, then passed a black stool; no further bleeding since. Two weeks of low-grade fevers and back ache. Open abdominal aortic aneurysm repair with a tube graft six years ago. Takes aspirin.

exam.abdomen: Healed midline laparotomy scar. Mild epigastric tenderness. No pulsatile mass. PR: melaena.

comorbidities: Abdominal aortic aneurysm — open repair with Dacron tube graft 6 years ago
surgicalHistory: Open infrarenal AAA repair, Dacron tube graft (6 years ago)

guideline.name: ESVS 2020 Clinical Practice Guidelines — management of vascular graft and endograft infections (aorto-enteric fistula)
guideline.section: Aorto-enteric fistula: suspect in any GI bleeding after aortic reconstruction; CT angiography first-line; endoscopy to exclude other sources without delaying treatment; urgent vascular surgical management
guideline.citation: Chakfé N, Diener H, Lejay A, et al. Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2020;59:339–384.

guideline.name: HALT-IT randomised trial — tranexamic acid in gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Tranexamic acid: no benefit, more venous thromboembolism
guideline.citation: HALT-IT Trial Collaborators. Effects of a high-dose 24-h infusion of tranexamic acid on death and thromboembolic events in patients with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (HALT-IT). Lancet. 2020;395:1927–1936.

rationale: Dangerous mimic of an ordinary ulcer bleed: the history of aortic graft surgery, fever and a self-limiting "herald" bleed should re-route the work-up to CT angiography and vascular surgery. An engine that treats it as peptic ulcer (PPI, OGD within 24 h) can lose the patient to the next, exsanguinating bleed.
